import base64
import json
import os

import requests

API = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OPENROUTER_API_KEY']}"}

def rows_schema(fields):
    """Wrap the fields of one row in a strict schema for {"rows": [...]}."""
    return {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {"rows": {"type": "array", "items": {
            "type": "object", "properties": fields,
            "required": list(fields), "additionalProperties": False}}},
        "required": ["rows"],
        "additionalProperties": False,
    }

def extract_table(pdf_path, schema, model="anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5",
                  engine=None, max_tokens=8000):
    with open(pdf_path, "rb") as f:
        data_url = "data:application/pdf;base64," + base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode()
    body = {
        "model": model,
        "max_tokens": max_tokens,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [
            {"type": "text", "text": "Extract every row of the table in this PDF. "
                                     "Include rows from every page. "
                                     "Return only rows that are in the document."},
            {"type": "file", "file": {"filename": os.path.basename(pdf_path),
                                      "file_data": data_url}},
        ]}],
        "response_format": {"type": "json_schema",
                            "json_schema": {"name": "table", "strict": True,
                                            "schema": schema}},
    }
    if engine:
        body["plugins"] = [{"id": "file-parser", "pdf": {"engine": engine}}]

    response = requests.post(API, headers=HEADERS, json=body, timeout=300)
    response.raise_for_status()
    data = response.json()
    choice = data["choices"][0]
    if choice["finish_reason"] == "length":
        raise ValueError(f"Output stopped at max_tokens={max_tokens}. "
                         "Raise it or split the PDF.")
    rows = json.loads(choice["message"]["content"])["rows"]
    if not rows:
        raise ValueError("No rows came back. If this PDF is a scan, use a model "
                         "that reads PDFs or engine='mistral-ocr'.")
    return rows, data["usage"]["cost"]

LINE_ITEMS = rows_schema({
    "sku": {"type": "string"},
    "description": {"type": "string"},
    "qty": {"type": "integer"},
    "unit_price": {"type": "number",
                   "description": "USD, no currency symbol or thousands separator"},
    "amount": {"type": "number",
               "description": "USD, no currency symbol or thousands separator"},
})
return 之前的两个检查会捕获第 3 步和第 4 步中涵盖的失败，因此请保留它们。成本来自 usage.cost，用量统计会在每个响应中包含它。

会在每个响应中包含它。

blocks.text: 模型写出的每一行都会消耗输出 token，所以长表格需要较高的 max_tokens。我们那份 58 行的发货日志根据模型不同使用了 2,500 到 7,700 个输出 token，这让最啰嗦的模型在 extract_table 中默认的 8,000 之下几乎没有余量。算下来每行是 43 到 133 个 token。对于长表格，从每个预期行约 150 个 token 开始。然后测量你自己的行，并保留 finish_reason 检查，因为计数会因模型和 schema 而异。下面是限制太低时会发生的情况。

blocks.text:
import base64
import json
import os

import requests

API = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OPENROUTER_API_KEY']}"}

def rows_schema(fields):
    """Wrap the fields of one row in a strict schema for {"rows": [...]}."""
    return {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {"rows": {"type": "array", "items": {
            "type": "object", "properties": fields,
            "required": list(fields), "additionalProperties": False}}},
        "required": ["rows"],
        "additionalProperties": False,
    }

def extract_table(pdf_path, schema, model="anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5",
                  engine=None, max_tokens=8000):
    with open(pdf_path, "rb") as f:
        data_url = "data:application/pdf;base64," + base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode()
    body = {
        "model": model,
        "max_tokens": max_tokens,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [
            {"type": "text", "text": "Extract every row of the table in this PDF. "
                                     "Include rows from every page. "
                                     "Return only rows that are in the document."},
            {"type": "file", "file": {"filename": os.path.basename(pdf_path),
                                      "file_data": data_url}},
        ]}],
        "response_format": {"type": "json_schema",
                            "json_schema": {"name": "table", "strict": True,
                                            "schema": schema}},
    }
    if engine:
        body["plugins"] = [{"id": "file-parser", "pdf": {"engine": engine}}]

    response = requests.post(API, headers=HEADERS, json=body, timeout=300)
    response.raise_for_status()
    data = response.json()
    choice = data["choices"][0]
    if choice["finish_reason"] == "length":
        raise ValueError(f"Output stopped at max_tokens={max_tokens}. "
                         "Raise it or split the PDF.")
    rows = json.loads(choice["message"]["content"])["rows"]
    if not rows:
        raise ValueError("No rows came back. If this PDF is a scan, use a model "
                         "that reads PDFs or engine='mistral-ocr'.")
    return rows, data["usage"]["cost"]

LINE_ITEMS = rows_schema({
    "sku": {"type": "string"},
    "description": {"type": "string"},
    "qty": {"type": "integer"},
    "unit_price": {"type": "number",
                   "description": "USD, no currency symbol or thousands separator"},
    "amount": {"type": "number",
               "description": "USD, no currency symbol or thousands separator"},
})
The two checks before the return catch the failures covered in steps 3 and 4, so leave them in. The cost comes from usage.cost, which usage accounting includes in every response.

inlines.text: Step 4: Why did my long table come back cut off?

blocks.text: Every row the model writes costs output tokens, so a long table needs a high max_tokens. Our 58-row shipment log used between 2,500 and 7,700 output tokens depending on the model, which left the most verbose model little room under the default of 8,000 in extract_table. That works out to between 43 and 133 tokens per row. For long tables, start with about 150 tokens per expected row. Then measure your own rows and keep the finish_reason check, since the count varies by model and schema. Here is what happens when the limit is too low.

blocks.text: When is a PDF library enough?

inlines.text: When is a PDF library enough?

blocks.text: If all your PDFs are digital and each table has a single header row, a free library such as pdfplumber will find the tables. We ran it on the same files. It found every table in the three digital PDFs and returned each cell as a string, such as ‘6,067.00’ or ‘(3,878)’. The quarterly report’s two-level header came back as two rows with None in the merged cells, and the shipment log came back as two separate tables, one per page. It found nothing in either scan, because a scan has no text layer to read.

blocks.text: Conclusion

Extracting a table from a PDF with an LLM takes one request, with the PDF as a file part and a strict schema that describes one row. In our tests, the accuracy came from a model reading the PDF directly, and the risk came from the route the PDF took. A text parser on a scan and a token limit on a long table both returned responses that looked normal. The two checks in extract_table catch both cases, so keep them in any version of the code you run. Before you settle on a route, run a sample of your own PDFs through it and compare the rows, the time and usage.cost.

inlines.text: Can an LLM read a scanned PDF?

blocks.text: Yes, if the model reads the PDF directly or you send it through the mistral-ocr parser. All three models that read PDFs got both of our scans right, and so did DeepSeek V4.1 Flash with mistral-ocr. A text parser such as cloudflare-ai returns an empty result for a scan with no error, because a scan has no text layer.

blocks.text: Will the model invent rows that aren’t in the PDF?

inlines.text: Will the model invent rows that aren’t in the PDF?

blocks.text: We didn’t see invented rows in 25 extractions of our five test PDFs, but that doesn’t rule them out on other documents. Missing rows were the bigger risk, caused by output cut off at the token limit or a parser that found no text. Compare the row count or a subtotal against the document.
